Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
227 AM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 226 AM EDT Tuesday...

A Frost Advisory is in effect for the Champlain Valley tonight.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 226 AM EDT Tuesday...

1. A cold day is expected today with a Frost Advisory for the 
Champlain Valley tonight. Gradual warming with some chances for 
light rain by Wednesday afternoon.

2. Dry and seasonable weekend before shower chances return for 
the beginning of next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 226 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Today will be a cool day in the upper 40s to mid 50s 
across the region. West to northwest winds will continue, but not so 
strong as yesterday. Max wind gusts this afternoon should top out 
around 20-25 mph, and higher summits will likely gust around 35-50 
mph much of the day. It will be dry, and despite the cool 
conditions, we should see relative humidity values fall down towards 
35 percent this afternoon. This isn't quite enough to push us 
towards fire weather concerns, but it is a bit close and a sign of 
the changing seasons. The dry conditions in place will mean that 
once winds drop off this evening, temperatures will quickly fall as 
radiational cooling initiates. It will fall into the mid 20s to mid 
30s across the region. The Champlain Valley remains in the 
Frost/Freeze program with the median first freeze around October 
11th. Grand Isle is less likely to observe frost, but just in case, 
threw the whole of the Champlain Valley in to a Frost Advisory for 
tonight. After about 5-6am, increasing south winds and cloud cover 
will end the frost potential.

During the day on Wednesday, we'll be at the southeastern periphery 
of a deep, mature low pressure that will set up near James Bay. Its 
warm front will cross east midday. Forecast soundings depict wide 
moisture spread. Given today's expected dryness, I'm inclined to 
think it will not rain Wednesday morning (precipitation falling as 
virga). In deference to some wetter solutions, there are some 10-30 
PoPs over the northern tier as the warm front crosses. Moderation 
behind the warm front will bring temperatures into the 60s, with 
perhaps a few holdouts in the upper 50s across the Northeast 
Kingdom. A prefrontal trough will approach the St. Lawrence River 
during the evening, and this could produce a few afternoon showers 
along the Route 11 corridor in far northern New York.

The actual cold front will arrive midday Thursday. It will bring 
rain showers in a fashion similar to today. A dynamic set up with 
modest 150-300 J/kg of instability will allow some convective 
elements. Although the upper level temperatures aren't quite as 
cool, there could be some pea sized hail as occurred yesterday, and 
a rumble of thunder cannot be ruled out either. Cool air will be 
reinforced behind the system, pushing nighttime lows back into the 
30s to lower 40s with a spot shower or two lingering while we remain 
under large scale cyclonic flow.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Troughing builds in for Friday with strong cold air 
advection continuing. While most of the moisture and dynamics from 
the upper low will remain to the north over Quebec, a brief 
shower/sprinkle is possible on Friday, mostly in the higher 
elevations. Snow levels are expected to fall below summit levels 
during this time, so a brief flurry or snow shower is possible in 
the highest peaks of the Adirondacks and Greens, but the lack of 
moisture would prevent anything more. Surface high pressure builds 
in for the weekend, leading to a classic fall stretch. Highs will be 
in the 50s and 60s with mostly sunny skies. As the high builds 
offshore to start next week, temperatures could get close to 70 in 
the valleys. A few showers will be possible early next week as 
another cold front makes a run at the region.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 06Z Wednesday...VFR conditions are expected to persist for
the next 24 hours. Winds will stay elevated through the morning,
with westerly gusts in the 10-20 KT range for most places. A couple
terminals, notably RUT and SLK, will lose gusts at times and only
have sustained winds around 10 KT. Winds will decrease during the
afternoon and by tonight, they should be mostly
light/variable/terrain driven. Winds become southerly in the later
part of tonight and tomorrow morning.

Outlook...

Wednesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Thursday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&
